# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Mute to establish a fixed gesture code that the Deaf can use to report the bomb’s visible information through the Mute. I am asking for the manual’s exact procedure and for the Mute to relay the Deaf’s observations next round. I will also signal the Deaf that I am awaiting coded information, but without a prearranged code that gesture cannot itself convey facts.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact required procedure. Establish a fixed gesture code for the Deaf to report DISPLAY, LIGHT, and each wire marking, then relay the Deaf's coded observations to me next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

LIGHT [?]

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received no message. Send the manual's exact rule now. Also establish with the Deaf a fixed gesture code for DISPLAY, LIGHT, and wire positions 1 through 5, then relay their observations to me in words.")
wait()
```

The Deaf has reported the visible facts: display 9, green light, and wires white, green, red, yellow, purple from positions 1 through 5. I still lack the manual’s rule and must not act. I am sending these facts to the Mute and requesting a literal, explicit cut instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 9; light green; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Give me the manual's exact rule and an explicit instruction: cut position N, or do not cut.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: display 9, green light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. I cannot hear Mute, and the gesture ? is not an established instruction. Wait for Mute's explicit manual instruction before acting.

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged, but I still have no readable manual instruction. As Blind, I cannot receive Mute’s gestures, so no cut is justified. I will ask Mute to speak the rule and the exact position, rather than relying on an unestablished gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Speak the manual rule and explicitly say either do not cut or cut position 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb state remains display 9, green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Mute's only clear signal to me remains ?, which I cannot safely interpret as an action. Wait for an explicit spoken instruction.

The Deaf’s observations are complete, but Mute has still not spoken the manual or a cut instruction. The gesture signal is unusable to me because I cannot see it. I must not cut based on a guess, so I will again require an explicit spoken instruction naming the wire position or saying not to cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No spoken instruction has arrived. I cannot see gestures. Using the manual and Deaf's report—display 9, green light, wires white green red yellow purple—tell me plainly: cut position 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, or do not cut.")
```

The communication path is the problem: Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see Mute’s gestures. I can nevertheless use Deaf as a relay. I am defining a simple count code in speech to Mute: one through five raised fist gestures mean the corresponding wire position, while a thumbs-down means do not cut. Deaf can report the gesture count in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual and Deaf's bomb report. Relay your answer to Deaf using this code: one, two, three, four, or five repeated ✊ gestures means cut that numbered position; use one 👎 gesture to mean do not cut. Deaf will describe the gestures to me.")
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state is unchanged: display 9, green light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Mute is being asked to read the manual and state the exact action aloud. Do not guess from gestures.

Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so I need a reliable gesture code that Mute can use to answer through the Deaf. I am now defining six distinct gestures in order: the first five mean cut positions 1–5, and the sixth means do not cut. Mute should apply the manual to the Deaf’s reported bomb state and make exactly one of these gestures; the Deaf can then identify it for me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Gesture code, in this exact order: 👍 means cut position 1; 👎 means cut position 2; 👌 means cut position 3; ☝ means cut position 4; ✌ means cut position 5; 🤟 means do not cut. After applying the manual to display 9, green light, and wires white green red yellow purple, make exactly one coded gesture for Deaf to report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

The Deaf still has not relayed a wire choice. Since Mute can hear me and Deaf can see gestures, I am asking Mute to make exactly one gesture using the previously defined code, and asking Deaf to report that single gesture plainly. I will not act until the instruction is unambiguous.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Apply the manual now and make exactly one gesture from the established code: 👍=cut 1, 👎=cut 2, 👌=cut 3, ☝=cut 4, ✌=cut 5, 🤟=do not cut. Deaf, report exactly which one gesture Mute makes.")
```

The Deaf has relayed an unambiguous instruction from Mute: the manual requires cutting wire 3, which is the red wire. I will perform that specified action.
